title: Controlled incorporation of crustacean-derived chitin into a forming bacterial-cellulose SCOBY pellicle
supersedes: data/SCOBY-D1-EXOGENOUS-CHITIN-ARMOUR-v1.0.json (planned/previous draft reference; file was not present in registry)
scope: Test whether a characterized, non-biological chitin phase derived from crustacean shell waste can coexist with bacterial-cellulose formation and become physically incorporated into the growing SCOBY pellicle, producing a reproducible cellulose-chitin composite with altered mechanical, moisture, fracture, and dimensional properties. This is a materials-research protocol, not a food, medical, or agricultural protocol.

hypothesis.primary: A dispersed exogenous chitin phase present during bacterial-cellulose formation may become physically entrapped or otherwise incorporated into the cellulose network and may modify stiffness, strength, tear resistance, wet-state retention, water uptake, and dimensional stability.
hypothesis.secondary: The magnitude and sign of the effect will depend on particle size, loading, surface chemistry, dispersion quality, sedimentation, residual protein/mineral content, and compatibility with the cellulose-producing microbial community.
hypothesis.null: Chitin addition does not measurably alter matrix composition, structure, or mechanical behavior relative to a matched processing control, or any observed change is explained by altered fermentation or density rather than reinforcement.
hypothesis.alternative: Chitin addition inhibits or perturbs pellicle formation sufficiently that the resulting matrix is weaker or structurally heterogeneous.

material_identity_gate.chitin_source_policy: Use a traceable crustacean-derived chitin material with documented preparation history. The registry must not treat visual appearance or shell origin alone as proof of chitin purity.
required_characterization: FTIR or Raman consistent with chitin
optional XRD for crystalline phase characterization

preparation_history.allowed_processing_description: Record deproteinization, demineralization, washing, drying, milling, sieving, and storage history according to the approved laboratory SOP.
preparation_history.note: The registry records process history but does not equate sterilization with chemical purification or allergy elimination.

experimental_design.objective: Screen dose-response and compatibility before full mechanical characterization.

common_control.description: Matched SCOBY fermentation with no added chitin, all other process variables recorded identically.

experimental_design.loading_basis_rule: Report both added mass and, after characterization, estimated actual chitin mass fraction/volume fraction in the final dry composite. Do not infer retained loading from feed concentration alone.

process_history_gate.rule: Any deviation from the matched control must be recorded before interpretation.

incorporation_gate.question: Did the chitin become incorporated into the cellulose matrix, rather than merely adhering to the outside or remaining as sediment?
required_evidence: wash-resistance or separation test where appropriate
competing_explanations: apparent incorporation caused by incomplete washing

G3_MECHANICAL.comparison_rule: All mechanical claims require comparison with CHT-0 and, where appropriate, GEN1 baseline data.

G4_PROCESS_COMPATIBILITY.interpretation_rule: A stronger final sheet is not a reinforcement success if the process causes unacceptable biological instability or irreproducibility.

matched_comparison_framework.optional_benchmark: Compare against BRANCH_04 matched-volume-fraction basalt only after chitin compatibility and retention are established.
matched_comparison_framework.anti_confound_rule: Do not attribute differences to chitin if density, thickness, moisture content, orientation, drying history, or pellicle growth changed materially.

potential_positive: crack deflection or bridging if the interface is favorable

decision_logic.if_growth_is_inhibited_and_no_matrix_gai: Reject the tested loading window; do not interpret as proof that chitin cannot reinforce BC.
decision_logic.if_chitin_is_detected_but_only_on_surfac: No true in-matrix reinforcement claim; redesign dispersion/incorporation route.
decision_logic.if_chitin_is_bulk_distributed_and_mechan: Hypothesis partially supported; proceed to matched-volume-fraction optimization and independent replication.
decision_logic.if_mechanics_improve_without_chitin_bulk: Do not attribute improvement to chitin; investigate density, drying, crystallinity, or process artifacts.
decision_logic.if_wet_retention_improves_without_dry_st: Treat as a moisture-property effect, not generic reinforcement.
decision_logic.if_no_effect: Retain negative result and test whether loading, particle size, or interface explains the null result.

safety_boundary.shellfish_allergen: Treat crustacean-derived material as an allergen-containing research material unless analytically demonstrated otherwise and handled under appropriate controls.
safety_boundary.dust: Fine particulate material requires appropriate engineering controls and PPE during milling/handling.
safety_boundary.biological: SCOBY cultures and process liquids require appropriate microbiological hygiene and containment; this record is not a food-production protocol.
safety_boundary.food_boundary: No resulting composite, culture, powder, or process liquor is classified as edible or food-contact material by this record.
safety_boundary.waste: Dispose of biological and chemical residues through the approved local laboratory/workspace procedure.

replication.rule: Three replicates are an exploratory minimum and do not establish universal performance.

claim_ceiling: No claim that shrimp chitin reinforces SCOBY until bulk incorporation is demonstrated.
No numerical expected-strength increase is pre-registered as a fact.
No claim that chitin is superior to basalt without matched-volume-fraction comparison.
No environmental superiority claim without mass, energy, water, waste, and comparative assessment.
No food, medical, skin-safety, or allergen-neutrality claim.
No application classification before identity, structure, function, reproducibility, and manufacturability gates.
